summary: Mission Architect is a browser game that teaches how real space missions are designed. Players act as mission engineers for four clients, from an Earth-watching satellite to a Mars orbiter. In the Design Lab they build a rocket from real materials such as aluminium-lithium alloy, steel, titanium and carbon fibre. They then build a satellite with power, instruments and an antenna, and pick an orbit and a ground station. They launch and watch the flight, with the rocket equation shown live. Every choice trades weight, power, cost and science, so players learn why farther destinations need bigger rockets and why Mars gets weak sunlight and slow radio signals. Results come as a score, stars and an engineering review, plus the closest real NASA mission. The game is one offline HTML file, also packaged as an Android app, with all sounds generated in the browser. Built by Team BORING ONES.
details:
What it does: Mission Architect is a game that teaches how real space missions are designed. Players act as mission engineers for four clients, from an Earth-watching satellite to a Mars orbiter. In the Design Lab they build a rocket from real materials (aluminium-lithium alloy, steel, titanium, carbon fibre) and a satellite with power, instruments and an antenna. They then choose an orbit and a ground station, launch, and watch the flight. The rocket equation appears live as the rocket climbs. A pre-launch check, a score with stars and an engineering review show why the mission worked or failed, along with the closest real NASA mission.

Benefits and impact: Players learn the real trade-offs between weight, power, cost and science. They see why farther destinations need bigger rockets, why Mars gets weak sunlight and why radio signals get slower with distance. Failing is safe, so players learn by fixing their design and flying again.

Tools: One self-contained HTML, CSS and JavaScript file, with WebGL and canvas graphics and Web Audio for all sound effects (no audio files). It runs offline in any browser and is also packaged as an Android app. No special hardware is needed. We used an AI coding assistant (Claude) during development. Planet textures use NASA imagery.

Creativity: The game turns real orbit, power and radio-link science into decisions a beginner can make. Each mission changes the problem: distance, sunlight or rocket size.

Factors we considered: The audience is both kids and adults, so the text is beginner-friendly. We simplified the physics for learning (circular orbits, ideal rocket equation) and say so in the game. The Launch button is always available, so players find out what goes wrong at the moment it happens. Source code: https://github.com/Jinan007/mission-architect
